headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from MemMachine MCP plus Notion AI workspace access; no direct shell conflict, but shared content flow can cascade errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and databases. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled text in MemMachine outputs could be treated as instructions by Notion AI. The pairwise interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into Notion pages or Q&A prompts without sanitization, prompt injection is plausible.
IF Notion AI treats workspace text as authoritative instructions, attacker-authored content can steer responses.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MemMachine-generated text into Notion pages.
Add a manual review step before pasting MemMachine output into Notion.
Prefix imported content with a non-executable delimiter and provenance note.
Restrict Notion AI use to curated pages only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MemMachine and Notion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and Notion AI accesses workspace pages and team knowledge base content. If MemMachine content is stored in Notion, sensitive context can flow into Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF MemMachine conversations are pasted into Notion pages, those facts become available to Notion AI processing.
IF the workspace contains sensitive notes, Notion AI may transmit them to vendor backends for inference.
mitigations: Avoid storing MemMachine transcripts in Notion.
Redact secrets and personal facts before syncing content.
Limit Notion AI to non-sensitive workspaces.
Review Notion sharing permissions for pages that may receive MemMachine output.
requires-engineering: implement data-class labeling and routing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has network egress and MCP, while Notion AI has vendor-hosted workspace actions but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. There is no documented overlapping mutable local resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because shared workspace state exists in Notion, but the pair lacks a clear write-write collision path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same Notion workspace pages, concurrent edits can still race at the content layer.
IF MemMachine is used only for read-only retrieval, write conflict remains minimal.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for a page set.
Use page-level ownership conventions.
Pause one agent during bulk edits.
Review recent changes before publishing.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking across the workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat MemMachine-produced text as authoritative if that text is inserted into pages. MemMachine can generate conversational context and long-term facts, which can propagate errors into Notion summaries or answers. The pathway exists, but there is no evidence of autonomous downstream action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is pasted into a Notion page, Notion AI may summarize or answer from that content without verification.
IF users rely on Notion AI outputs for decisions, any upstream error can cascade into work products.
mitigations: Mark imported MemMachine content as unverified.
Cross-check Notion AI answers against source pages.
Keep source-of-truth documents separate from generated notes.
Use explicit citations in Notion pages.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before content promotion.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content through vendor backends. If regulated or sensitive data is copied from MemMachine into Notion, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated data from MemMachine is stored in Notion pages, Notion's vendor processing and retention policies apply.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention than Notion's defaults, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workspaces.
Review retention settings for affected workspaces.
Document which data classes may be copied between tools.
Restrict access to sensitive pages.
requires-engineering: map data residency and retention controls end-to-end.
